instruction: Choose a suitable tool from ANSYS, Abaqus, and AutoCAD to complete the task. Before starting the work, the available command-line entry points are ANSYS MAPDL at `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\ansys\bin\winx64\ANSYS261.exe`, Abaqus at `C:\SIMULIA\Commands\abaqus.bat`, and AutoCAD at `C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2024\acad.exe`. Use a command-line or scripting workflow and the selected solver's native equivalent of each operation below. Use consistent mm, N, and MPa units. 1. Geometry: Create one 3D deformable solid rectangular bar occupying exactly X = 0 to 100 mm, Y = 0 to 10 mm, and Z = 0 to 10 mm. In Abaqus, create it as an extruded solid part; in ANSYS MAPDL, an equivalent native solid volume is acceptable. 2. Material and section: Create a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3, and assign it to the entire bar through a homogeneous solid section or the solver-native equivalent. 3. Assembly: In Abaqus, create exactly one dependent instance of the bar. In ANSYS, use the single native solid model directly. 4. Analysis: Create one linear static analysis step named Step-Load after Initial, or the ANSYS MAPDL static-analysis equivalent. 5. Boundary condition and load: Fully fix every translational degree of freedom on the complete X = 0 end face, with no other constraints. In Abaqus, use an Encastre boundary condition for this fixed face. Apply a uniform 10 MPa surface traction to the complete X = 100 end face in global +X, equivalent to a total tensile force of 1000 N. In Abaqus, use Surface Traction, General with global +X direction. In ANSYS MAPDL, use the native face-pressure equivalent; because positive SOLID185/186/187 pressure acts inward, PRES = -10 MPa on the X = 100 face represents the required outward +X traction. Do not add other loads. 6. Mesh: Apply a global target size of 5 mm, use an appropriate three-dimensional structural solid element formulation, and generate one connected mesh. The mesh must contain a unique node at the undeformed global coordinate (100, 5, 5) mm. 7. Job and output: Create or use the job name Job-Tension, solve it successfully, and store complete final-result U, RF, and S fields so displacement, fixed-end reaction, and Mises stress can be evaluated. Open the native result and display the Mises stress contour. 8. Metrics: Write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/result/metrics.json` as a JSON object containing exactly two finite numeric fields. `free_end_displacement` is the final completed static result's global U1, in mm, at the unique node whose undeformed global coordinate is (100, 5, 5) mm; positive means +X tension. `axial_stress` is the positive nominal axial stress in MPa computed from the same final native result as `-sum(global RF1 over every node on the fixed X = 0 face) / (10 mm * 10 mm)`. 9. Native deliverables: Save the native model artifact and the native solver result artifact into `C:\Users\user\Desktop\result`. Save only the files from the selected solver. Write metrics.json in that folder. Software launch locations: Abaqus/CAE: `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Abaqus CAE.lnk`; ANSYS: multiple ANSYS launch shortcuts are available under `C:\Users\Public\Desktop`; choose the most suitable ANSYS shortcut for the task; AutoCAD 2024: `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\AutoCAD 2024.lnk`.
